title: HelperFSListResult
description: Result of the helper fs service's list op: one page of one directory, with the facts a client needs to paginate and to poll. Entries is never null — an empty directory is [] — because a decoder must not have to tell 'no rows' from 'no answer'.

path.description: The lexical path the caller asked about, echoed.

canonical.description: The provider-canonical identity of the directory actually listed. Returned for every successful list, not only for symlinks, so the root and every ordinary ancestor speak one identity vocabulary.

entries.description: The page's rows, in the provider's order. Never null.

offset.description: The offset this page answered, echoing the request.

total.description: How many entries the complete directory holds, not how many this page carries.

hasMore.description: Whether the complete listing holds entries after this page.

rev.description: The digest of the WHOLE, ordered directory (filesystem.ComputeRev): every entry's name, size, mtime, mode, kind, link target and link kind, plus the canonical identity of the directory itself. Two polls compare digests instead of re-reading every row, and a changed digest means the client re-lists once and replaces the page atomically.

entry.description: One row. Path is LEXICAL — the absolute spelling joined onto the directory the caller asked about, symlinks unresolved — so the tree a client draws keeps the shape it requested; Canonical describes the directory actually read.

name.description: The entry's name, never a path.

path.description: The entry's lexical absolute path: the caller's directory spelling plus this name.

kind.description: The kind of object, in internal/filesystem.Kind's own closed vocabulary: `regular`, `dir`, `symlink`, `other` (a FIFO, socket or device) or `unreadable` (the entry exists but its metadata could not be read).

linkTarget.description: Present exactly for a symlink: the target as the link states it, which may be relative to the link's directory.

linkKind.description: Present exactly for a symlink: what the target IS. `other` means the link is genuinely broken, `unreadable` means the target exists but could not be classified — different facts a person acts on differently.

size.description: The object's size in bytes. Zero is a real size.
